youtube.title: Wood Frog: Why Does Its Heart Stop Every Winter?
youtube.description:
The wood frog freezes solid every winter: no heartbeat, no breath, ice right under its skin. And then it comes back to life in spring.

As ice forms on its skin, the frog's liver floods its cells with glucose, a natural antifreeze, so the ice stays outside the cells. Up to 70 percent of its body water can freeze. In Alaska, scientists found wood frogs that stayed frozen for more than six months at temperatures down to minus 18 degrees Celsius, and every single one survived.

scenes.text: This frog's heart stops every winter.
scenes.visual: Hook frame on a snowy spruce forest floor: a wood frog (tan, banded folded legs, dark mask stripe through the eye) sits pale with frost inside a cracked, frosted block of ice on the leaf litter; a red heart on top of the block beats, then on 'stops' turns grey, cracks and a red flatline runs out under it; the fez host stands big on the right in shock; snow falls, a snow bank with a fallen snowy log fills the bottom.

scenes.text: In Alaska, the wood frog freezes solid.
scenes.visual: Wide shot of an Alaskan spruce forest in falling snow: the wood frog sits in brown leaf litter in the middle; on 'freezes' a pale frost film spreads over its body, its eyes turn cloudy white and a big ring of ice crystals blooms around it; red card 'ALASKA'; a fallen snowy log and big leaves in the foreground.

Close-up of the frozen frog in the snow, ice sparkles all over its skin: above it a red heart-monitor line beats and goes flat on 'heartbeat'; small breath puffs from its nostril stop on 'breath'; hand label 'NO HEARTBEAT'.

The fez host leans in and prods the frozen frog with a long twig; on 'was' the stiff frog tips over onto its back like a stone, the twig drops and the host jumps back in shock; red card 'DEAD?'; snowy forest, fallen log in front.

scenes.text: So what's the trick? As ice forms, its liver floods every cell with sugar.
scenes.visual: In a lab under a hanging lamp, a big cut-away drawing of the frog lies on a tray on the bench: ice sparkles appear on its skin on 'ice'; on 'liver' a 'LIVER' card pops up with a red arrow to the dark red liver, which glows gold; on 'sugar' thick bright gold sugar dots stream along the veins into the whole body; gold card 'SUGAR'.

scenes.text: Sugar works like antifreeze and keeps the ice out of its cells.
scenes.visual: Full-frame view through a microscope eyepiece: round cells fill with gold sugar dots; on 'ice' blue ice crystals grow in the gaps between the cells and stop at the cell walls; cards 'SUGAR' and 'ICE'.

scenes.text: Up to 70 percent of its body water turns to ice,
scenes.visual: The wood frog sits big in the snowy forest; pale blue ice rises inside its body from the feet up to a red dashed mark at 70 percent while a big red counter above runs from 0 to '70%'.
The frozen frog lies on the forest floor under a growing snow mound; a tear-off calendar nailed to a spruce trunk on the right flips its pages month by month, NOV to MAY; red card '6+ MONTHS'.

scenes.text: Then spring comes, and its heart beats again.
scenes.visual: Spring at a pond edge: snow patches melt, water drips off the frog as its frost fades and its gold eyes clear and blink; on 'heart' a big red heart pops above it and beats with gold rays; reeds, lily pads and ripples on the pond, grass in front.

scenes.text: Subscribe for a wild true story every day.
scenes.visual: At the spring pond: the fez host stands on the left and waves, then points at the viewer on 'story'; the wood frog sits on the bank on the right, croaking with a puffing throat; reeds and lily pads behind, grass in front.
